name: Jehdeiah
title: Levite and Covenant Sealer
summary: Jehdeiah was a Levite who lived in the period following the return from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one who helped the people understand God's law and sealed the covenant to follow the Lord's commands. The name Jehdeiah means 'the glory of the Lord' and is borne by several individuals in the Old Testament.

keyEvents.title: Teaching of God's Law
keyEvents.description: Jehdeiah was among the Levites who helped the people understand the law when Ezra read it aloud to the assembly.

keyEvents.title: Leadership in Prayer and Praise
keyEvents.description: Jehdeiah led the people in prayer and praise during the great assembly of repentance after the law had been read.

keyEvents.title: The Sealing of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Hodija was one of the Levites who sealed the covenant, where the people committed themselves to keeping God's law and commandments.

keyEvents.title: The People's Oath of Loyalty
keyEvents.description: As part of entering into the covenant, Hodija and the other leaders pledged to follow God's law given through Moses, and to avoid intermarriage and Sabbath violations.

keyEvents.title: Participation in Rebuilding the Community
keyEvents.description: Hodija took part in the spiritual renewal and rebuilding of the Jewish community in Jerusalem after returning from Babylon.
